newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen's troops set to capture last royalist town.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen's troops set to capture last royalist town.

text.p: Forces loyal to Cambodian coup-leader Hun Sen were within a few kilometres of this last royalist-held town on Monday and may capture it within days, Cambodian and Thai sources said.

Residents scrambled to bury, pack up or sell off their possessions in preparation for evacuation as soldiers loyal to ousted co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh exchanged mortar and rocket fire with Hun Sen's forces some 12 km (seven miles) away.
Thai army sources said it was only a matter of time before Hun Sen's troops took this last town under royalist control.
"I think Hun Sen troops will overrun O'Smach by tonight," one army officer said.

Ranariddh, toppled by Hun Sen in a coup on July 6, abandoned plans to visit the border area soon after his arrival in Bangkok on Saturday after Thai officials expressed reservations about using Thai territory for political ends.

Many royalist officials and supporters fled from Cambodia to Thailand after the prince was toppled and after a subsequent crackdown in which some 40 of the prince's supporters were killed, according to U.N. human rights officials.

The prince's troops were pushed out of Phnom Penh over two days of fighting in early July and have gradually been pushed back to this remote northwest region which Ranariddh held before a U.N. peace settlement in the early 1990s.
Many of the 15,000 Cambodian refugees in this town were seen preparing to evacuate as the sound of mortar and rocket fire was audible from areas deeper inside Cambodia.
"People living here have buried their valuables and are set to evacuate. We can unearth and retrieve them later," Srey Rodmai, 32, a father of three, told Reuters.
A royalist officer said Hun Sen troops had already taken Samrong town, 30 km (20 miles) from here, and were now facing his forces at Jakraom village, about 12 km (seven miles) from O'Smach.
Traders who have sought shelter in this border town have sold off their goods cheaply as royalist forces began firing mortars and rockets in apparent defence of their line.

"I paid 200 baht for this but I think the price will come down to 100 baht later today when there is more gunfire from here," a Thai man who went to buy two items of military camouflage from the Cambodia traders said.
The only Cambodian doctor running a makeshift hospital here housing 69 patients with malaria and other illnesses was optimistic the royalist forces would be able to hold on.
"Hun Sen said he would capture O'Smach by today but I don't think he can do it. I don't believe in Hun Sen's childish remarks," Sit Thee told Reuters.
However he said he had laid plans to evacuate his patients in case Hun Sen's forces do overrun the border town.
About 10,000 people, mostly Cambodian traders, lived in O'Smach before Hun Sen's takeover in Phnom Penh and many said they had no plans to join the 15,000 recent arrivals if they fled to Thailand.

"The people who had been living here have no plan to run away, even if Hun Sen troops come in we can live with them. But for those newly arrived they may have to find other places to live," a Cambodian trader, who asked not to be named, said.
A Thai army officer said an evacuation site has been prepared for the Cambodian refugees.
